# `starhermit:ui`

Engine **1.41.0** (host API 1.41), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:ui";
```

The engine's immediate-mode UI for the game's own menus and HUD panels: call widgets every frame (from `onUpdate` or `onRender`) and they return what the player did. It lays out, draws into the overlay (after `starhermit:draw`), takes pointer, touch, keyboard (Tab, arrows, Enter, Escape) and gamepad navigation (D-pad or left stick, South to activate, East to go back), follows the player's UI scale, text size, contrast and reduced-motion settings (see `preferences`), and builds an accessibility tree screen readers read. Labels are the widgets' identities unless `id()` names them, so keep them stable or set ids for translated labels. At most 4,096 widgets a frame (RangeError). A click or tap needs its press and its release on the same widget, each counted where it happened, so one that comes and goes between two frames (a quick tap on a slow frame) still clicks; a frame clicks at most once, and further taps between two frames click in the frames after it, in order.

Sizes. What the game passes is logical pixels: theme sizes, text sizes, padding, spacing, and layout, paragraph, slider, field, progress, image and scroll-area sizes. Each frame the UI multiplies them by `preferences().scale` (the window's scale factor times the player's interface size) and text sizes by `textScale` on top, as the runtime's own menu does; a change the player makes in the Options menu shows on the next frame. What the UI returns is window pixels: rectangles, scroll offsets, `measureText`. Rectangles the game gives (`setViewport`, `area`) are window pixels too. A game that places widgets itself measures them with `measureText` (never `starhermit:draw`'s, which is unscaled) and divides window pixels by `scale` for the logical sizes it passes back: a column as wide as its widest label is `{ width: widest / ui.preferences().scale }`; a screen-filling one is `frame().width / ui.preferences().scale` wide, not `/ frame().scale`.

Fonts. Text draws with the default faces (`system-ui`), `setFont`'s family or a text option's (`TextOptions.font`), each falling back as `starhermit:draw`'s text does: the system's faces, then the engine's emoji font and pixel font. Emoji draw in colour from the engine's own emoji font, StarHermit Emoji, loaded the first time text needs it; until then they keep their room and draw nothing, and measured widths (`measureText`) are already theirs. Single emoji and keycaps (`2️⃣`) only in this version: ZWJ sequences draw as their emoji one by one, skin tones are dropped, flags draw as regional indicator letters (see "Emoji" in `starhermit:draw`).

### Rect

*interface*

A widget's or container's rectangle (window pixels): a new frozen object each call, so one the game keeps never changes.

```ts
export interface Rect { … }
```

- `readonly x: number;`
- `readonly y: number;`
- `readonly width: number;`
- `readonly height: number;`

### Align

*type*

```ts
export type Align = "start" | "center" | "end";
```

### Layout

*interface*

```ts
export interface Layout { … }
```

- `padding?: number | { top?: number; bottom?: number; start?: number; end?: number };`

  Logical pixels; one number for all sides.

- `spacing?: number;`

- `align?: Align | "stretch";`

  Across the axis; `"stretch"` (since API\_MINOR 12) gives every child the container's whole width (a column's) or height (a row's): in an auto-sized column, its widest child's. In a `grid`, where cells sit in their row's height (`"stretch"`: as tall); in a `stack`, where children sit across it (`"stretch"`: its whole box).

- `justify?: Align | "space-between" | "space-around" | "space-evenly";`

  Along the axis: the children together at the start, center or end, or (since API\_MINOR 12, CSS `justify-content`) the free space between them: `"space-between"` between each two (one child stays at the start), `"space-around"` a share around each (half a share at the ends), `"space-evenly"` equal shares between them and at the ends. The free space is the container's size (fixed, filled, stretched or grown) less its children's last frame, so a content-sized container has none. In a `stack`, where children sit down it.

- `` width?: number | `${number}%`; ``

  The outer size, padding and border included (CSS `box-sizing: border-box`), as a style's `width` and `height`. Since API\_MINOR 26 also a percentage (`"50%"`) of the container's content box, as in CSS: where that box's size depends on its content (a column without a fixed width, a content-sized row, a scroll area's content), the percentage is `auto`. A container's box is known along an axis when it has a fixed size there, or fills, stretches or grows to one; the top level's is the area below the origin. In a grid it is the cell's width. Older minors warn and ignore a percentage.

- `` height?: number | `${number}%`; ``

- `wrap?: boolean | "wrap" | "nowrap" | "wrap-reverse";`

  A row's children flow onto new lines when it is full (since API\_MINOR 26; CSS `flex-wrap`): `true` or `"wrap"` adds lines below, `"wrap-reverse"` above (the first line at the bottom). A wrapping row without a `width` fills its container's width (as a CSS block-level flex container), so a wrapping row in a row is one line unless it has a width. Lines break on this frame's sizes; `align` places children within their line's height (`"stretch"`: as tall), and `justify` spreads each line's free space. A line's height and spread come from last frame where the frame is not past it yet, so a line whose content changes size settles on the next frame, as a grid's rows do. Tab order follows the lines as they show, top to bottom (a reversed row's last line first); arrows move by position. Columns ignore it. Older minors warn and ignore it.

- `gap?: number | { row?: number; column?: number };`

  A row's gaps (since API\_MINOR 26): one number for both, or `column` (between children in a line, as `spacing`) and `row` (between wrapped lines; default the column gap). A grid's own `gap` is as before.

- `background?: ColorLike;`

  The panel's color (the theme's opaque panel under high contrast).

- `clip?: boolean;`

  Clip children to the container.

- `text?: TextOptions;`

  The text of everything inside (since API\_MINOR 8): smaller type for a wide table, a handwritten face for a letter. Nested containers and widgets' own options override it.

- `style?: string | readonly string[];`

  The container's classes (since API\_MINOR 12), as `style()` gives them: it is styled as a `panel` with a background, else a `row` or `column`.

- `grow?: number;`

  A share of the free space along the enclosing container's axis (since API\_MINOR 12, CSS `flex: 1`): its height in a column of fixed height (or the root column, the viewport's), its width in a row of fixed width, split between growing children by their shares. The free space is what the other children took last frame (on its first frame, what is left after the children before it). In a container without a fixed size it has no effect.

- `role?: "radiogroup";`

  `"radiogroup"` (since API\_MINOR 12): a segmented control. The buttons inside with `selected` (and `widget`s of role `"radio"`) are its radios, announced "radio, 2 of 3" with the group's label: one stop for Tab (the chosen radio, else the first), arrows along its axis move to the next or previous radio and choose it (the button activates, as a click would), and leave the group at its ends; the other arrows leave it as a block.

- `tooltip?: Tooltip;`

  The container's tooltip (since API\_MINOR 12), as a widget's.

### TextOptions

*interface*

A widget's or container's text (since API\_MINOR 8); each option absent keeps the enclosing container's (else the theme's).

```ts
export interface TextOptions { … }
```

- `size?: number;`

  Logical pixels, for every text style (labels, headings, buttons): the player's UI scale and text size settings still enlarge it, and it is at least 10 (smaller sizes draw at 10). A widget's own `size` and `font` win over the text its style class sets, as an inline style over a class; a scope's (`ui.text`, a container's options) are inherited, so a class's text still wins inside it.

- `font?: string;`

  A family added with `canvas.fonts` (any case), a generic family (`system-ui`, `sans-serif`, `serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `fantasy`: the system's faces, as `starhermit:draw` maps them) or `starhermit pixel`, or since API\_MINOR 37 `StarHermit Emoji` (the engine's emoji font first: see "Emoji" in `starhermit:draw`); absent with a `weight`, the UI's own family (`setFont`'s, else `system-ui`). Another name throws a TypeError. The runtime bundles no handwriting face: `cursive` is the system's (Comic Sans MS on Windows, as browsers pick; elsewhere and on the web runtime the sans-serif faces), so a game wanting handwriting everywhere adds its own font. At most 64 families and weights a game (RangeError).

- `weight?: FontWeight;`

  A number from 1 to 1000, as text too, `"normal"` or `"bold"` (see `FontWeight`; a family without a bold face draws a synthesized bold at 600 and more).

Where the UI lays out (window pixels; default the whole window less its safe area). It may change during a frame: widgets after a call lay out in the new area (see `area`).

### area

*function*

```ts
export function area(rect: Rect, build: () => void): Rect;
```

Lays out `build`'s widgets in another window rectangle this frame (several regions a frame: a chat field in one corner, a toggle in another), then returns to the current area.

Names the next widget or container (focus and state survive a changed label). Returns the module for chaining: `ui.id("play").button(label)`.

### lastRect

*function*

```ts
export function lastRect(): Rect | null;
```

The rectangle (as the call returned it, window pixels) of the widget or container placed last this frame (since API\_MINOR 26; older minors throw a TypeError): a container's once its `build` returned, so after `ui.row(…)` it is the row's. It is this frame's layout, as the call returned it (sizes measured from this frame's content, a few things such as a wrapping line's height or a grid row from last frame). Null before anything is placed this frame. Useful for anchoring a game drawing to a widget whose call returns no rectangle.

## Layout (since API\_MINOR 12)

The box model is CSS's `box-sizing: border-box`: a container's or widget's `width` and `height` are its outer size, border and padding included. A container without them is as large as its content (its children's own sizes and margins, plus its padding and border), at least its style's `minWidth` and `minHeight`; `width: "fill"`, `align: "stretch"` and `grow` give a child the room its container has instead (a column's width, a grid cell, a stack's box), and its content size still counts what it needs, so a stretched column shrinks again when its widest child does. Placement that needs a size not known yet (justify, centring, `auto` grid columns, a row's height for its cells) uses last frame's, so a new layout settles on its second frame; rows above the one being built are this frame's, so cells never overlap the rows before them. Right to left, start and end swap: rows, grid columns, anchors, margins and alignment mirror.

### GridTrack

*type*

```ts
export type GridTrack = number | "auto" | { fr: number };
```

A grid column's or row's size: logical pixels, `"auto"` (its widest cell last frame; tallest for a row), or `{ fr }`, a share of the room the others leave (CSS `minmax(0, 1fr)`). A column may also be `{ width, align }` (`width` pixels or `"auto"`) or `{ fr, align }`: where its cells sit across it (`"stretch"`: as wide), CSS's `td:last-child { text-align: right }` being `align: "end"` on the last column.

### GridColumn

*type*

```ts
export type GridColumn =
  | GridTrack
  | { width?: number | "auto"; fr?: number; align?: Align | "stretch" };
```

### GridLayout

*interface*

```ts
export interface GridLayout extends Layout { … }
```

- `columns: number | readonly GridColumn[];`

  A count of equal shares, or the columns (at most 64, RangeError). A grid with `fr` columns and no `width` fills its container's width (as CSS's block-level grids), and in a row (no width to share) they size as `"auto"`.

- `rows?: readonly GridTrack[];`

  Row sizes from the top (at most 64); rows past them are `"auto"`. `fr` rows share a fixed `height`.

- `gap?: number | { row?: number; column?: number };`

  Logical pixels between cells (default the layout's `spacing`).

- `rowStyle?: string | readonly string[];`

  Classes of a box drawn behind each row, the grid's whole width (ruled rows, zebra stripes, a hovered row): its state blocks `first`, `last`, `odd` and `even` say which row, `hoverWithin` the pointer over it.

- `cellStyle?: string | readonly string[];`

  Classes of a box drawn behind each cell, its whole area (column rules, cell backgrounds), `first`, `last`, `odd` and `even` by its column.

### grid

*function*

```ts
export function grid(label: string, build: () => void, layout: GridLayout): Rect;
```

A grid (CSS `display: grid`): its children fill its cells row by row from the start (`cell` places one elsewhere or spans columns). Tab and screen readers go in build order, so build cells in reading order; arrows move from cell to cell. A child's `first`, `last`, `odd` and `even` state blocks match its column in its row. Styled as `grid` (as `panel` with a background).

### cell

*function*

```ts
export function cell(cell: { column?: number; row?: number; span?: number }): typeof import("starhermit:ui");
```

Where the grid's next child goes: its `column` and `row` (from 0; absent, the next free one), and how many columns it `span`s (default 1). A column alone goes in the current row unless the cells before it are past it (then in the next row); with a row, the cell is exactly there and the cells after it carry on where they were. A cell spanning columns does not size `auto` columns. Outside a grid it throws a TypeError. Returns the module for chaining: `ui.cell({ span: 2 }).label("Total")`.

### gridRow

*function*

```ts
export function gridRow(classes: string | readonly string[]): typeof import("starhermit:ui");
```

Classes for the box behind the grid row its next child goes in (since API\_MINOR 12), after the grid's `rowStyle`: a row of its own look, as the player's gold-edged row of a leaderboard. Call it before the row's first cell; its state blocks (`first`, `odd`, `hoverWithin`…) work as `rowStyle`'s. Outside a grid it throws a TypeError. Returns the module for chaining: `ui.gridRow("me").label(name)`.

### stack

*function*

```ts
export function stack(label: string, build: () => void, layout?: Layout): Rect;
```

Children over each other in one box (a badge on an icon, a caption on a picture): each sits by the stack's `align` across and `justify` down (`align: "stretch"` gives each the whole box). The box is its largest child's (or its `width` and `height`). Tab and screen readers go in build order. Styled as `stack` (as `panel` with a background).

### Anchor

*type*

```ts
export type Anchor =
  | "top-start" | "top" | "top-end" | "start" | "center" | "end"
  | "bottom-start" | "bottom" | "bottom-end";
```

### place

*function*

```ts
export function place(
    label: string,
    at: Anchor | { anchor?: Anchor; x?: number; y?: number },
    build: () => void,
    layout?: Layout,
  ): Rect;
```

A column anchored in the inner box of the container it is built in, out of that container's flow (CSS `position: absolute`): a badge on a stack's corner, a close button at a panel's top end, at the top level a HUD piece in a corner of the screen (inside its safe area). `x` and `y` (logical pixels) move it in from the edges it is anchored to (on an axis it is centred on, toward the end and the bottom); its style's margin does the same. `{ x, y }` alone is from the top-start corner. Its size is its content's: in the frame that changes (its first, new content) it is laid out at the old size, then moved, input and focus included, to where the anchor puts it. It stays in the focus order where it is built. In a stack it counts toward the stack's size; elsewhere it takes no room. Since API\_MINOR 18 the topmost takes the pointer, by last frame's rectangles (later is on top): a placed container with a background or a style (a pause card over a board), any container with one in a stack, and a scroll area take the pointer (hover, presses, the wheel) over their whole box from what was built before them under it, and an interactive widget from those under its own rectangle. A placed container painting nothing (an effects layer drawn over the UI, a widget of role "none") lets the pointer through between its interactive widgets. Games declaring an older minor keep the earlier rule: the first widget built under the pointer takes it.

### spacer

*function*

```ts
export function spacer(share?: number): Rect;
```

An empty child taking a `share` (default 1) of the free space along a row or column of fixed size, as `grow` does for a container (CSS's `flex: 1` spacer): the brand at a header's start, the stats at its end. Its Rect spans the row's height (the column's width), so the room a fixed-height column leaves is a region to draw in (a game's view under a HUD); that span is not content, so it never widens a column sized by its children. A non-positive share throws a RangeError.

### Tone

*type*

```ts
export type Tone = "normal" | "muted" | "accent" | "danger";
```

A tone colors a label's text from the theme (`"muted"`, `"accent"`) or by an explicit color (the theme's text color under high contrast).

### Tooltip

*type*

```ts
export type Tooltip = string | (() => void);
```

A tooltip (since API\_MINOR 12): text, or a function that builds its content with widgets (labels, headings, images, meters: presentation, interactive widgets throw a TypeError), called on the frames it shows. It shows by the widget's rectangle (below it from its start edge, above it when there is no room below, inside the window's safe area) once the pointer rests on the widget 0.6 seconds, and at once while the widget has keyboard or gamepad focus; a press hides it until the pointer leaves. Text tooltips are the widget's accessible description always; built ones while they show. Styled by the `tooltip` kind; one shows at a time. Widgets take it as their `tooltip` option, or the next widget from `ui.tooltip(…)`.

### image

*function*

```ts
export function image(alt: string, texture: Texture, size: { width: number; height: number }, uv?: { min: [number, number]; max: [number, number] }, options?: WidgetOptions): Rect;
```

`size` (logical) is the image's own; styled as `image` (or by a chained `style`), the style's padding and border go around it and the image fills what they leave (so a style's fixed size stretches it). `uv` (0–1 from the texture's top-left) reaching outside the texture draws what lies inside it, the box shrinking with it, as `draw.image`'s `source` does (since 1.16.5; before, a region a hair outside was clamped and one further out left out).

*function*


The next widget's tooltip (since API\_MINOR 12; see `Tooltip`). Chains: `ui.tooltip("Costs $1,200").button("Office")`.

### ButtonOptions

*interface*

True on the frame it was activated. A disabled button shows muted, stays in the focus order for screen readers (announced unavailable) and never activates. An activation by a press counts as that press for `clipboard.writeText` and pointer lock during this frame.

```ts
export interface ButtonOptions extends TextOptions, WidgetOptions { … }
```

- `disabled?: boolean;`
- `tone?: Tone;`

- `ariaDisabled?: boolean;`

  Announced unavailable and styled by the `disabled` state block, but still activates (since API\_MINOR 12): a locked tool that says why when pressed.

- `selected?: boolean;`

  A toggle (since API\_MINOR 12): announced pressed or not, styled by the `selected` state block (the active tool, the chosen segment). In a `radiogroup` container, a radio of the group instead.

- `content?: () => void;`

  Builds the button's face (since API\_MINOR 12): an icon over two lines, a title with a small second line, a stat chip. It runs in a column inside the button's padding (aligned by the style's `text.align`, centered vertically in a taller button); what it builds is presentation (it takes no focus or input; an interactive widget throws a TypeError) and is styled as the button is: its state blocks and `inside` rules match the button's state (`".tool": { inside: { label: { selected: { … } } } }`), and its text takes the button's text color. The button stays one widget: one focus stop, activated by a click anywhere on it, Enter, Space or South. Its accessible name is `label`, and the content's text its description; with an empty `label` (give it an `id`) the content's text is its name.

### button

*function*

```ts
export function button(label: string, options?: ButtonOptions): boolean;
```

### checkbox

*function*

```ts
export function checkbox(label: string, checked: boolean, options?: WidgetOptions & { appearance?: "box" | "switch" }): boolean;
```

Returns the value after this frame's input. `appearance: "switch"` (since API\_MINOR 12) draws a pill whose knob sits at the end when checked (the parts `box` and `mark`, round unless a style says otherwise); it is announced as a checkbox.

### slider

*function*

```ts
export function slider(label: string, value: number, options: WidgetOptions & { min: number; max: number; step?: number; width?: number }): number;
```

Arrows step by `step` (default a hundredth of the range); since API\_MINOR 12 a press or drag lands on `min + k × step` too, within the range. Styled as `slider`, its parts `track` and `thumb`, and since API\_MINOR 22 `fill`: the track from `min` to the value (from the right, right to left, as the track mirrors), as a browser fills a range in its `accent-color`. It takes the track's paint (background colors and gradients, radius, border, shadow) and draws only when a style gives it a look (`parts.fill`, or CSS `accent-color` and `::-moz-range-progress`); under high contrast it takes the focus color, as the thumb does. A game declaring an older minor draws no slider fill, whatever its styles say.

### SelectOption

*type*

```ts
export type SelectOption = SelectOptionFields & ({ text: string; label?: string } | { text?: string; label: string });
```

An option of a select as an object (since API\_MINOR 12): its text, an icon before it, whether it is disabled. It has `text`, `label` or both, as HTML's `<option>`: the `label` is what shows (and is announced) unless it is empty, else the `text` (`{ text: "Ivy", label: "" }` shows Ivy). `label` is accepted since engine 1.20.2 (any minor; earlier engines throw a TypeError). Any other shape, or a `text` or `label` that is not a string, throws a TypeError.

### SelectOptionFields

*interface*

The fields of a `SelectOption` besides its text.

```ts
export interface SelectOptionFields { … }
```

- `icon?: Texture | null;`

  Drawn before the text; null or left out for none.

- `disabled?: boolean;`

  Shown in the muted color and announced unavailable, never chosen: the arrow keys and the D-pad pass over it, and clicks, taps and assistive activation on it do nothing (since API\_MINOR 14; a graphics level above `frame().levelCeiling`). The index passed in may still be one: it shows as the choice.

- `description?: string;`

  Read after the text by assistive technology: why it is disabled (since API\_MINOR 14).

### select

*function*

```ts
export function select(label: string, index: number, options: readonly (string | SelectOption)[], extra?: WidgetOptions): number;
```

A dropdown; returns the chosen index. Styled as `select`, its parts `field` (the closed control), `list` (the open list) and `option` (each option: `hovered` under the highlight, `selected` the current choice). Since API\_MINOR 33 a styled select lays out by its style as CSS sizes a `select`: `width` (or `"fill"`, or a percentage of its container), `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `height` and `minHeight` (CSS `width`, `max-width` and the rest); narrower than its widest option, the shown option is cut at its content box and the open list stays as wide as that option (within the window). Before, it was always as wide as its widest option whatever its style said, as older games keep it. The open list's options scrolled out of it are offscreen to assistive technology, not part of a scroll area the select is in.

### cycle

*function*

```ts
export function cycle(label: string, index: number, options: readonly string[], extra?: WidgetOptions): number;
```

Left/right arrows through the options; returns the index.

### textField

*function*

```ts
export function textField(id: string, value: string, options?: WidgetOptions & { maxChars?: number; width?: number; placeholder?: string; arrows?: boolean }): string;
```

Returns the edited text (at most `maxChars`, default 256). `placeholder` shows while it is empty. While it has focus the runtime takes text input at its caret: typing, input method compositions (shown at the caret; scripts' `text` events get the committed text only) and paste (Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert natively; in browsers, through a text entry the page puts over the field until it loses focus). In browsers that focused text entry is a real one, so on phones and tablets tapping a text field brings up the on-screen keyboard (a text keyboard whose Enter reads Done; the tap's release focuses it within the gesture, as iOS asks), its typing, suggestions and deletions reaching the field, and leaving the field puts it away. The runtime reads the clipboard for a paste, never the game: the pasted text arrives as typed text does (a `text` event, then the field's new value), on one line (trailing line breaks dropped, the others spaces), at most 64 KiB natively. No capability is needed. While it has focus the field has the keyboard (`capturingKeys()` is true): since API\_MINOR 17 the keyboard presses no actions meanwhile. Arrows and the D-pad reach a field only from focus the player sees (navigating the UI), never from nothing focused or from a press, since API\_MINOR 17 (older games: as any widget); `arrows: false` (since API\_MINOR 17) keeps them out always: Tab, a press, `setFocus` and screen readers still focus it (a chat field beside a game steered with the arrows). Styled (`style(...)`, the `textField` kind), since API\_MINOR 23 it lays out as CSS lays out an input: its style's text size, padding and border around the line, `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `width` (or `"fill"`) and `height` (CSS `min-height` and the rest), the line centred in a taller box; `width` here is its width otherwise. Before, a style only painted it: the field stayed one theme line high and `width` wide whatever the style's sizes, padding and text size, as older games keep it. The player selects as in a browser's input (every API minor): a double click selects the word under the pointer, a triple click the whole text, dragging a press selects a range, Control+A (Command+A on macOS) selects everything, and Shift with the arrows, Home and End extends the selection; Control with the arrows (Option on macOS) moves by words, and Command with them to the ends on macOS. The selection draws highlighted: typing, pasting, an IME composition, Backspace and Delete replace it, and a move or click collapses it. Control+C or Control+Insert copies it and Control+X or Shift+Delete cuts it (Command on macOS): the runtime puts the text on the clipboard (no `clipboard` capability needed; the game cannot read it), and the game hears the keys and a cut's change to the value.

### submitted

*function*

```ts
export function submitted(id: string): boolean;
```

Whether Enter was pressed in the text field `id` this frame (the field keeps focus; `setFocus(null)` leaves it).

### tabs

*function*

```ts
export function tabs(label: string, index: number, labels: readonly string[], content: (index: number) => void): number;
```

Tab strip plus the chosen tab's content; returns the chosen index. Styled as `tabs` (each tab), its parts `strip` (the box behind the tabs) and `tab` (each tab over the kind's look).

### ScrollAreaRect

*interface*

A scroll area's rectangle and, since API\_MINOR 8, its scroll state after this frame's input, in window pixels like the rectangle (the DOM's names): `scrollTop` from 0 to `scrollHeight - clientHeight`, `scrollLeft` toward the content's end (leftward right-to-left), `scrollHeight`/`scrollWidth` the content as this frame built it, and `clientHeight`/`clientWidth` the part showing it (less the scroll bar).

```ts
export interface ScrollAreaRect extends Rect { … }
```

- `readonly scrollTop: number;`
- `readonly scrollLeft: number;`
- `readonly scrollHeight: number;`
- `readonly scrollWidth: number;`
- `readonly clientHeight: number;`
- `readonly clientWidth: number;`

### ScrollAreaOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface ScrollAreaOptions { … }
```

- `scrollTo?: { top?: number; left?: number; behavior?: "instant" | "smooth" };`

  Moves the content this frame (since API\_MINOR 8; window pixels, as reported): a Next page button sets `top: r.scrollTop + r.clientHeight`, a log stays at its end with `top: Infinity`; past the end stops there, before the start at 0, and NaN throws a TypeError. An absent axis stays. `"instant"` (default) moves it this frame, `"smooth"` glides as the wheel does (instant with reduced motion). It ends a drag of the area. Pass it only on the frame it should move. A frame hears its input first (`onAction` listeners run before `onUpdate` and `onRender` build the widgets), while an area's state is known only once its `scrollArea` call returned: a `scrollTo` worked out from this frame's result moves the content on the next call, a frame late. Work it out in the action listener from the last frame's result (keep it), and pass it on this frame's call.

- `style?: string | readonly string[];`

  Classes (since API\_MINOR 12): the `scrollArea` kind's style and these draw its box behind the content.

- `grow?: number;`

  Takes a share of the free space along its container's axis instead of `size`'s height (width in a row), as `Layout.grow` (since API\_MINOR 12).

- `padding?: number | { top?: number; bottom?: number; start?: number; end?: number };`

  The content's inset inside the area's clip (since API\_MINOR 12, CSS padding on a scrolling box), logical pixels: room for its children's focus rings and shadows, which the clip cuts at its edges. Without it, a styled area takes its style's padding and border.

### scrollArea

*function*

```ts
export function scrollArea(label: string, size: { width: number; height: number }, build: () => void, options?: ScrollAreaOptions): ScrollAreaRect;
```

Content taller (or wider) than `size` scrolls by wheel, drag, its bar, focus moving inside, and the game (`options.scrollTo`).

### dialog

*function*

```ts
export function dialog(label: string, title: string | null, open: boolean, build: () => void): boolean;
```

A modal dialog while `open`: input reaches nothing behind it. Returns whether it is still open (Back or Escape closes it). Styled as `dialog`: its style is the panel (its padding and border hold the title and content, since API\_MINOR 12), its part `backdrop` the dim over the screen behind it. `title` is its heading above `build`'s content and its accessible name. Since API\_MINOR 17 an empty or null title draws no heading: the content starts at the top of the padding (a game's own title, or something above it), and screen readers name the dialog by `label`, so make `label` readable (games declaring an older `engine.minor` keep a heading: empty, or `"null"`).

### back

*function*

```ts
export function back(): boolean;
```

Back (Escape, East) pressed this frame and not taken by a dialog.

### capturingKeys

*function*

```ts
export function capturingKeys(): boolean;
```

The UI has the keyboard, as the last frame ended: a text field has focus or a key capture waits for a key. Game shortcuts read from keys should wait. Since API\_MINOR 17 the keyboard presses no actions meanwhile (`onAction`, `isDown`; releases still come, so nothing stays held, and `key` events still do); older games hear them and hold them back themselves.

### pointerOver

*function*

```ts
export function pointerOver(): boolean;
```

Whether the pointer is over a widget (the game should not act on its clicks). A `target` is none: it takes nothing, so the pointer over it is the game's (earlier releases read true over a button target). It tests where the pointer is against each widget's own rectangle, as the UI last drew it (read while this frame's UI is being built, only the widgets built so far count). A finger has no hover: its pointer is where it pressed or last lifted, and the UI aims a finger's press at the nearest widget within a touch-sized target (44 logical pixels), so a tap just beside a small widget presses it while this says false. To tell whether a click or tap went to the UI, use `pointerCaptured`.

### pointerCaptured

*function*

```ts
export function pointerCaptured(): boolean;
```

Whether this frame's press of the primary pointer (a mouse's primary button, or the first finger) went to the UI: true from the frame it came in through the frame of its release (a tap down and up within one frame reads true in that frame), else false. A press goes to the UI on a widget (a finger's within the touch-sized target the UI aims it at, so a tap beside a small button that presses it counts), on a box the UI painted (a background or style) or a scroll area, or anywhere while a modal `dialog` or an open `select` list takes all input; a `target` takes none. It is decided as the press comes, against the UI the last frame built, as the UI's own widgets decide, so it reads the same in `onPointerButton`, `onTouch`, `onUpdate` and `onRender`, before or after the frame's widgets: a game's board skips a click or tap whose frame reads true. A finger on an on-screen touch control (`setTouchControls`) is never the UI's. Since API\_MINOR 23.

### focused

*function*

```ts
export function focused(): string | null;
```

The focused widget's label as the last frame ended (null when nothing had focus); the same all through a frame (since API\_MINOR 12: before, it was null once the frame's first widget was built).

### target

*function*

```ts
export function target(text: string, rect: Rect, options?: { role?: "button" | "label" }): void;
```

Names an area the game draws itself (since API\_MINOR 17): a Canvas 2D game's button shown with `draw.image`, a board's tile. It is a node of the UI's accessibility tree named `text` over `rect` (window pixels, clipped as widgets built where it is: in a scroll area, out of view when scrolled away), a button or, with `role: "label"`, text that only reads, and it lays out, draws, focuses and takes nothing: the pointer over it stays the game's (`starhermit:input`), so the game's own hit tests answer clicks there. Play scripts (`click TEXT`, `until TEXT`) find it as they find a widget, so a game need not draw its labels as overlay text to be tested. Call it every frame the area shows, like a widget (it counts toward the widgets a frame); its identity is `id()` or `text`. A rect that is not an object, or another role, is a TypeError.

Screen readers, and in browsers the page's ARIA mirror of the UI (a layer of elements over the canvas, each at its widget, which automation such as Playwright's getByRole finds by role and name and clicks), see every widget with its role, name and states, and focus and activate widgets as the player does, whatever minor the game declares.

### announce

*function*

```ts
export function announce(text: string, options?: { politeness?: "polite" | "assertive" }): void;
```

Has the player's screen reader speak `text` (since API\_MINOR 9): what a game drawn without widgets cannot say otherwise ("hal played Nf3, check", "Checkmate — you won"). Natively a UI Automation notification (Windows) or an AT-SPI announcement (Linux); in browsers a live region on the page. Works at any time (an action or socket handler, a frame without widgets, nothing focused), the runtime's menu open or not. `"polite"` (default) waits until the reader finishes what it is saying; `"assertive"` interrupts it, for news that cannot wait. At most 500 characters (RangeError; another politeness is a TypeError); an empty or blank text says nothing. Four announcements are spoken at once, then one each half second: past that only the newest waits (a polite one never replaces a waiting assertive one) and the rest are dropped, so announce what changed, not every frame. A frame keeps at most four: past them each new one replaces the frame's oldest polite one (an assertive one the oldest assertive one when all are; a polite one among only assertive ones is dropped), as a live region keeps its latest text, and the console warns once. However many a frame announces, `announce` never throws for it (a runtime before 1.20 threw "RangeError: too many requests this frame" past the frame's 64 requests). Players without a screen reader hear nothing.

### setFocus

*function*

```ts
export function setFocus(name: string | null): void;
```

Focuses a widget from the next frame (null: none), with its focus ring, as keyboard focus is: a scroll area holding it scrolls it into view. `name` is a widget's `ui.id`, else its label (its accessible name): the first focusable widget whose id it is, else the first whose label it is, so one widget's id wins over another's label. It names the widgets of the frame it is called in, before or after they are built; when that frame has none, the next frame's (the screen the game switches to), unless focus moved elsewhere meanwhile. Within an open modal dialog, only its widgets.

Since API\_MINOR 20 keys go to the game unless a widget has focus, as keys go to a browser's page unless a focusable element has it: the keyboard's arrows never focus a widget from nothing focused, so the arrows and Enter stay a board cursor's until the player gives the UI focus (Tab, a press on a widget, the gamepad's D-pad or stick, this call, a dialog opening), and a press on no widget outside a modal dialog takes focus away. Older games' arrows focus the first or last widget from nothing focused, and such a game calls `setFocus(null)` to give the keys back.

### setLanguage

*function*

```ts
export function setLanguage(tag: string, direction?: "ltr" | "rtl"): void;
```

The language widgets announce (BCP 47) and its direction (right-to-left mirrors the layout); default the player's language.

### lang

*function*

```ts
export function lang(tag: string, build: () => void): void;
```

A subtree in another language.

### Theme

*interface*

Colors (sRGB) and sizes (logical pixels) over the player's settings: the player's interface and text sizes multiply the sizes, and a high-contrast setting replaces the colors (white text and outlines on black, yellow accent and focus), also when the theme is set during a frame. Each call changes what it names and keeps the rest of the game's theme.

```ts
export interface Theme { … }
```

- `fontSize?: number;`
- `headingSize?: number;`
- `smallSize?: number;`
- `padding?: number;`
- `spacing?: number;`
- `text?: ColorLike;`
- `muted?: ColorLike;`
- `panel?: ColorLike;`
- `control?: ColorLike;`
- `hovered?: ColorLike;`
- `pressed?: ColorLike;`
- `field?: ColorLike;`
- `accent?: ColorLike;`
- `focus?: ColorLike;`
- `outline?: ColorLike;`

- `radius?: number;`

  The corner radius of styled widgets and panels (since API\_MINOR 12; default 0). Unstyled widgets stay square.

### setTheme

*function*

```ts
export function setTheme(theme: Theme): void;
```

## Styles (since API\_MINOR 12)

Looks a game registers once (`setStyles`) by widget kind (`"button"`) and class (`".primary"`), and widgets name each frame (`style()`), so menus can look like the game's original HTML and CSS while focus, keyboard, gamepad, touch, screen readers and the player's settings keep working. A widget's look is, in order, later winning: the theme's defaults for its kind, the game's kind style, the `inside` rules of its enclosing containers (outermost first), its classes in the order given, and inline styles; then, for each of its states, the state blocks of those in the order first, last, odd, even (where it is among its container's children), hoverWithin, focusWithin, hovered, focused, focusVisible, checked, selected, pressed, disabled (CSS's practical precedence: a selected tool keeps its look under the pointer, a press shows while held, disabled wins over all), whichever rule gave the block: a kind's `hovered` loses to an `inside` rule's `selected`. Each property replaces what came before it (`background`, `shadow` and `decorations` as a whole, as in CSS), except `padding`, `border` and `text`, whose fields merge. Sizes are logical pixels. Sizes are border-box (CSS `box-sizing: border-box`): a style's or layout's `width` and `height` are the outer size, padding and border included, so a port of content-box CSS adds the padding and border to its widths. On widgets that hold text they are minimums (text never cuts: it grows the box, or ellipsizes with `text.overflow`).

The player's settings apply last and win: the interface size scales every size (borders stay at least a pixel), the text size scales text, and high contrast forces colors as CSS `forced-colors` does: one solid fill by role and state (panels and controls black, hovered and pressed greys, selected the theme's selection blue), white text (grey when disabled), white borders at least 1 wide on controls (yellow when focused or selected), no shadows, decorations in the text color, opacity 1, and a yellow focus ring at least 3 wide even where a style says `"none"`. Shapes, sizes, fonts and spacing stay.

Styles are checked when registered: an unknown key or a value of the wrong shape throws a TypeError (a typo CSS would ignore), a bound a RangeError, and a call that throws registers nothing. A class named with no style registered draws as if unnamed, with one warning in the console (none for a class some `inside` rule names). Tokens are checked where used: one missing or of the wrong kind leaves that property as it was, with one warning. Styles are resolved once per combination of rules and state and cached, so a frame's widgets cost a lookup each; register them once, not per frame.

Widgets: buttons, labels, headings and paragraphs lay out and draw whole by their style (padding, border, sizes, box and text). Containers (`column`, `row`, `panel`, `scrollArea`, `dialog`) draw their box behind their children and take its padding. `checkbox`, `slider`, `progress`, `meter`, `select`, `cycle`, `textField` and `tabs` (each tab) take the box behind them, the text color and the focus ring, and since API\_MINOR 12 their parts (`parts`: the slider's `track` and `thumb`, and since API\_MINOR 22 its `fill`, the track from `min` to the value, drawn only when a style names it; the checkbox's `box` and `mark`, the select's `field`, `list` and `option`, progress bars' and meters' `track` and `fill`, the tabs' `strip` and `tab`, the dialog's `backdrop`, a scroll area's `track` and `bar`) take their own; a part no style gives a look keeps the theme's.

The focus ring shows for focus the player sees (CSS `:focus-visible`, since API\_MINOR 12): focus moved by the keyboard, a gamepad, `setFocus` or a screen reader. A press or tap focuses the widget without it. `focused` matches any focus, `focusVisible` only the former.

Boxes past a frame's budget (131,072 mesh vertices of styled boxes; repeating gradients take the most) draw without unblurred outer shadows from the next frame, then without gradients (their first color), never without content or inset and blurred shadows (baked as images, they take no vertices). The log warns the first time.

### WidgetKind

*type*

```ts
export type WidgetKind =
  | "panel" | "column" | "row" | "label" | "heading" | "paragraph" | "image"
  | "progress" | "button" | "checkbox" | "slider" | "select" | "cycle"
  | "textField" | "tabs" | "scrollArea" | "dialog"
  | "widget" | "tooltip" | "meter" | "document"
  | "grid" | "stack";
```

The widget kinds a style key names.

### Token

*type*

```ts
export type Token = `$${string}` | `var(--${string})`;
```

A token's name where its value goes: `"$gold"`; since API\_MINOR 26 also a custom property's, `"var(--gold)"` or `"var(--gold, #fc0)"` (see `CustomProperties`).

### Length

*type*

```ts
export type Length = number | Token;
```

A number in logical pixels, or a token for one.

### PartName

*type*

```ts
export type PartName =
  | "track" | "fill" | "thumb" | "box" | "mark" | "field" | "list"
  | "option" | "strip" | "tab" | "backdrop" | "bar";
```

The parts of compound widgets (`Style.parts`, since API\_MINOR 12).

### Sides

*interface*

Per side: `start` and `end` follow the language's direction.

```ts
export interface Sides<T> { … }
```

- `top?: T;`
- `end?: T;`
- `bottom?: T;`
- `start?: T`

### Corner

*type*

```ts
export type Corner = Length | { cut: Length };
```

A corner: a radius, or a straight cut this far along each side (CSS `clip-path` chamfers).

### Corners

*type*

```ts
export type Corners = Corner | readonly [Corner, Corner, Corner, Corner] | Token;
```

One corner for all four, or start-top, end-top, end-bottom, start-bottom. Corners on a side that would overlap shrink together, as in CSS.

### Stop

*type*

```ts
export type Stop = ColorLike | { color: ColorLike; at?: number | readonly [number, number] };
```

A gradient stop: a color, spread evenly, or one `at` 0–1 (a repeating gradient's: logical pixels). Since API\_MINOR 12 `at` may be two positions, a stop at each (CSS's `#ffcc33 0 5px`).

### LinearGradient

*interface*

```ts
export interface LinearGradient { … }
```

- `type: "linear";`

- `angle?: number;`

  Degrees, as CSS: 180 (default) top to bottom, 90 start to end.

- `stops: readonly Stop[];`

  2 to 16 stops (RangeError). As CSS: the first defaults to 0, the last to 1, missing ones spread between their neighbors; colors mix premultiplied, so `transparent` fades.

- `repeating?: boolean;`

  Repeats (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `repeating-linear-gradient`): the stops' `at` are logical pixels along the gradient line, the last one given (TypeError), and the pattern repeats every last less first: stripes, scanlines, brushed metal. A hard stop (two colors at one place) changes over one pixel, so stripes' edges are smooth; a period under 2 window pixels (or more than 2,048 stops over the box) draws as its average color instead of shimmering.

### RadialGradient

*interface*

```ts
export interface RadialGradient { … }
```

- `type: "radial";`

- `center?: { x: number; y: number };`

  Fractions of the box (default 0.5, 0.5).

- `radius?: { x: number; y: number } | "farthest-corner" | "closest-side";`

  Fractions of the box, or CSS's extents (default `"farthest-corner"`).

- `shape?: "ellipse" | "circle";`

  `"ellipse"` (default, the box's proportions) or `"circle"`.

- `stops: readonly Stop[];`

- `repeating?: boolean;`

  Repeating rings (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `repeating-radial-gradient`): `at` in logical pixels along the horizontal radius, as `LinearGradient.repeating`. Rings are drawn as polygons at each stop, a quarter of a pixel at most inside their curves (they were drawn on a grid of up to 96 cells a side, several times the vertices); a box of rings that would take more vertices than such a grid draws on the grid, so very fine ones blur.

### ImageFill

*interface*

An image filling the box (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `background-image`): a Texture (a loaded one: a Texture still loading throws a TypeError when the style is registered) or an image file of the game's by its path (PNG or WebP, loaded on first use and drawn from the frame after it is ready; a missing or broken file is warned once and draws nothing). The image counts against the game's image budget. It is clipped to the box's corners, its edges antialiased. A style or token holds its Texture while it names it (the game need not keep it), and the Texture's `needsUpdate` shows in the style from that frame, as in a material: a repainted CanvasTexture or new DataTexture data. A canvas resized gets a new image: the keys naming it are registered again with it (keys that `extends` one keep the old image until they are registered again).

```ts
export interface ImageFill { … }
```

- `image: Texture | string;`

- `region?: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };`

  The part of the image, in its pixels (an atlas region).

- `size?: "auto" | "cover" | "contain" | readonly [number, number];`

  `"auto"` (default: the image's own size, a pixel of it a logical pixel), `"cover"`, `"contain"` or \[width, height\] in logical pixels, as CSS `background-size`.

- `position?: { x: number; y: number };`

  Where the image sits in the free room, fractions (default the center), as CSS `background-position`.

- `repeat?: boolean | "x" | "y";`

  Tiles it across both axes (`true`), one (`"x"`, `"y"`) or none (default), from `position`; past 256 tiles it is drawn once, stretched over the box.

- `tint?: ColorLike;`

  Multiplies the image (default white).

### SliceFill

*interface*

An image nine-sliced over the box (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `border-image`): frames and plates. `slice` cuts the image (its pixels, top, right, bottom, left as CSS lists them, or one for all) into corners drawn at their size, edges stretched along the box's sides and a middle drawn (stretched) only with `fill`. `width` is how wide the slices draw, logical pixels (default the slices' own sizes, a pixel a logical pixel); slices wider than the box shrink together. Not clipped to the box's corners, as CSS's.

```ts
export interface SliceFill { … }
```

- `image: Texture | string;`
- `slice: number | readonly [number, number, number, number];`
- `width?: number | readonly [number, number, number, number];`
- `fill?: boolean;`
- `region?: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };`
- `tint?: ColorLike;`

### Fill

*type*

```ts
export type Fill = ColorLike | LinearGradient | RadialGradient | ImageFill | SliceFill;
```

A color, a gradient, an image (since API\_MINOR 12), or a token (`"$name"`) for one. High contrast draws every layer as one solid color.

### Shadow

*interface*

CSS `box-shadow`: logical pixels; `blur` as CSS's (a Gaussian of deviation blur / 2), at most 128 (RangeError). Blurred and inset shadows are baked once into images that count against the game's image budget (16 MiB of them at most, the least recently used let go). An inset shadow draws only inside the box. Since API\_MINOR 20, as in browsers, an outer shadow draws only outside the box's (rounded or cut) border edge, so a translucent background never shows it through (a focus ring made of `spread` stays a ring); before, it draws under the whole box too, showing through a translucent background.

```ts
export interface Shadow { … }
```

- `x?: Length;`
- `y?: Length;`
- `blur?: Length;`
- `spread?: Length;`
- `color: ColorLike;`

- `inset?: boolean;`

  Inside the box (bevels, wells, a one-pixel highlight).

### TextStyle

*interface*

```ts
export interface TextStyle { … }
```

- `color?: ColorLike;`

- `size?: Length;`

  Logical pixels (at least 10; the player's text size on top).

- `font?: string;`

  A family added with `canvas.fonts`, a generic family or a token.

- `weight?: FontWeight | Token;`

  A number from 1 to 1000 (`700`), as text too, `"normal"` or `"bold"` (see `FontWeight`), or a token.

- `` letterSpacing?: number | `${number}em` | Token; ``

  Extra logical pixels after each character, or `"0.12em"`.

- `transform?: "none" | "uppercase" | "lowercase" | "capitalize";`

  What draws only: screen readers hear the text as written.

- `align?: "start" | "center" | "end";`

  Where the text sits in the widget's content box; a paragraph's lines each.

- `numerals?: "proportional" | "tabular";`

  `"tabular"`: every digit takes the widest digit's advance.

- `variant?: "normal" | "small-caps";`

  `"small-caps"` (since API\_MINOR 26; CSS `font-variant`): lowercase letters draw as capitals at 0.7 of the size on the same baseline, synthesized whatever the font (its `smcp` glyphs are not used); the text read to assistive technology keeps its case. Single-line text only: wrapped text keeps its case. Older minors warn and ignore it.

- `shadow?: Shadow | readonly Shadow[] | Token;`

  Text shadows, drawn under the text, the last lowest (at most 4; CSS `text-shadow`): an offset, a color and (since API\_MINOR 12) a `blur` up to 32 (RangeError; no `spread` or `inset`), a glow for LED text. A blurred one is baked once into an image (keyed by the text, face, size and blur) and counts against the image budget, as box shadows do; text that changes every frame bakes every frame, so keep glows for labels that hold still. Wrapped text (a paragraph) draws its blurred shadows unblurred. High contrast drops them.

- `stroke?: { width?: number; color?: ColorLike } | "none";`

  An outline around each glyph, under its fill (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `-webkit-text-stroke` with `paint-order: stroke`, at twice the width): `width` logical pixels out (at most 4, RangeError), drawn as the text 4 or 8 times around. High contrast drops it.

- `fill?: LinearGradient | "none";`

  A linear gradient filling the text instead of `color` (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `background-clip: text`): across the text's box, baked once into an image like a glow. Wrapped text draws in its first color. High contrast drops it.

- `overflow?: "visible" | "ellipsis";`

  `"ellipsis"`: text wider than the widget's width (its style's `width`, else its column's) is cut with "…", after `maxLines` lines (default 1). The whole text stays the widget's accessible name.

- `maxLines?: number;`
- `opacity?: number;`

### Decoration

*interface*

A shape in the box (CSS `::before`/`::after` with absolute position): an accent bar, a rule, a corner bracket, a chevron. Each edge is logical pixels in from that side of the box; `width`/`height` fix its size (a missing edge is 0 unless the size and the other edge place it; with both edges and the size, the size is centred between them, as CSS's inset with `margin: auto`: `{ top: 0, bottom: 0, height: 9 }` stays vertically centred however tall the box grows). It has a `fill`, a `border` or both. At most 8 a style.

```ts
export interface Decoration { … }
```

- `fill?: Fill;`

- `border?: { width?: Length | Sides<Length>; color?: ColorLike };`

  A border-only shape (since API\_MINOR 12): a chevron is a square with a `top` and `end` border, turned 45 degrees. Width 1 unless given.

- `radius?: Corners;`
- `top?: Length;`
- `bottom?: Length;`
- `start?: Length;`
- `end?: Length;`
- `width?: Length;`
- `height?: Length;`

- `rotate?: number;`

  Degrees clockwise about its center (since API\_MINOR 12; mirrored right to left). Its blurred shadows turn with it since API\_MINOR 13 (games declaring an older `engine.minor` keep them upright).

- `shadow?: Shadow | readonly Shadow[] | Token;`

  Its glows and shadows, as a box's (since API\_MINOR 12; outer only).

- `over?: boolean;`

  Over the content instead of under it.

- `opacity?: number;`

  Multiplies its alpha, 0–1 (since API\_MINOR 12; a chevron fading in on hover).

### BoxStyle

*interface*

```ts
export interface BoxStyle extends CustomProperties { … }
```

- `background?: Fill | readonly Fill[];`

  Fill layers, first on top (at most 4).

- `border?: { width?: number | Sides<number>; color?: ColorLike | Sides<ColorLike>; style?: "solid" | "double" };`

  `style: "double"` draws two lines a third of the width each.

- `radius?: Corners;`

- `shadow?: Shadow | readonly Shadow[] | Token;`

  Outer and inset shadows, first on top (at most 6).

- `padding?: Length | Sides<Length>;`

  Inside the border; part of `width` and `height` (border-box).

- `margin?: Length | Sides<Length>;`

  Room outside the box (since API\_MINOR 12), logical pixels: it keeps the box from its siblings and its container's edges, and counts in its container's size. Negative margins pull it out: into its container's padding (`.console h2 { margin: 0 -14px }`, a full-bleed header band, a divider or tab strip across a padded panel, with `width: "fill"`), or over the sibling before it. A clipped container still clips at its padding. The margin comes from the style without its interaction states (layout doesn't move on hover; structural blocks such as `first` apply).

- `` minWidth?: Length | `${number}%`; ``

  Since API\_MINOR 26 `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `width`, `height`, `maxWidth` and `maxHeight` also take a percentage (`"50%"`) of the container's content box (see `Layout.width`): `auto` where that box depends on its content (a minimum then is 0, a maximum none).

- `` minHeight?: Length | `${number}%`; ``

- `` maxWidth?: Length | `${number}%` | "none"; ``

  At most this outer size (since API\_MINOR 26): pixels, a percentage or `"none"`. A minimum wins over a maximum, as in CSS.

- `` maxHeight?: Length | `${number}%` | "none"; ``

- `` width?: Length | `${number}%` | "fill"; ``

  The outer width (border-box), at least, or `"fill"`: the whole width of the column it is in (since API\_MINOR 12 also its grid cell's or stack's), less its margins. A column without a width is as wide as its widest child, so `"fill"` in it fills only that: give the column a `width`, or `align: "stretch"` in a column that has one. In a row it has no effect.

- `` height?: Length | `${number}%`; ``
- `opacity?: number | Token;`

- `translate?: { x?: number; y?: number };`

  Moves what draws (logical pixels); the widget still lays out, hits and focuses where it is (a hover lift without jitter).

- `scale?: number;`

  Scales what the box draws, its children included, about its center (since API\_MINOR 12; 0–16, RangeError past it; CSS `scale`). Drawing only, as `translate`.

- `rotate?: number;`

  Turns what the box draws about its center, degrees clockwise (since API\_MINOR 12; mirrored right to left; after `translate`, as CSS composes them). Since API\_MINOR 13 everything turns, as a CSS transform turns an element: shapes, text (with its shadows, glows, strokes and gradient fills), images, nine-slices and blurred shadows, edges antialiased; boxes turned inside turned boxes add up. Games declaring an older `engine.minor` keep text, images and blurred shadows upright (they move with the turn). A game-drawn widget's own drawing (`draw`) stays upright. Drawing only.

- `transition?: number | Transition | readonly Transition[] | "none";`

  How the look's values move when they change (since API\_MINOR 12; see `Transition`). The look changed to gives it, as in CSS.

- `animation?: Animation | "none";`

  A keyframe animation (since API\_MINOR 12; see `Animation`).

- `text?: TextStyle;`
- `decorations?: readonly Decoration[];`

- `focusRing?: { color?: ColorLike; width?: number; offset?: number; radius?: Corners } | "none";`

  The focus indicator (CSS `:focus-visible` outline): `offset` outside the box (negative inside), or `"none"` (high contrast draws one anyway).

- `backdropBlur?: number;`

  Blurs what is behind the box (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `backdrop-filter: blur()`), logical pixels, at most 32 (RangeError): the 3D scene and what the overlay drew before it, as a Gaussian of that deviation, in the box's shape, under its background (glass panels, a dialog's `backdrop` part). At most 4 a frame, within twice the window's area; past them, at low graphics quality, and where the renderer has no room for its copy of the frame (a half or a quarter of the window, three images), the box draws its tint instead: its first background color at least half opaque (black at 35% without one). The scene under it is drawn again at that size without shadows or post effects, which the blur hides. High contrast turns it off.

### StateStyles

*interface*

Box and text properties for a state (no nested states or `inside`).

```ts
export interface StateStyles { … }
```

- `first?: BoxStyle;`

  Where it is among its container's children (since API\_MINOR 12; CSS `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:nth-child(odd)` and `(even)`, counting from 1): in a grid, its column in its row (a grid's `rowStyle` boxes: their row). `last` is the last of last frame's children (a list that grows settles on its next frame). In `inside` rules too: `inside: { label: { last: { text: { align: "end" } } } }`.

- `last?: BoxStyle;`
- `odd?: BoxStyle;`
- `even?: BoxStyle;`

- `hovered?: BoxStyle;`

  The pointer over it (never a finger: since API\_MINOR 13 also not the pointer a platform moves with the first finger, so nothing stays hovered after a tap; a mouse or pen hovers).

- `pressed?: BoxStyle;`

  Held down: by a mouse or pen while its button is held, wherever the pointer goes; by a finger (since API\_MINOR 13) only while it is down on the widget.

- `focused?: BoxStyle;`

  Any focus: keyboard, gamepad, pointer or a screen reader.

- `focusVisible?: BoxStyle;`

  Focus the player sees (since API\_MINOR 12, CSS `:focus-visible`): by keyboard, gamepad, `setFocus` or a screen reader, not a press.

- `disabled?: BoxStyle;`

  A disabled or `ariaDisabled` button.

- `checked?: BoxStyle;`

  A ticked checkbox, a checked widget, a chosen select option.

- `selected?: BoxStyle;`

  The chosen tab, a `selected` button, a chosen select option.

- `hoverWithin?: BoxStyle;`

  Containers: the pointer over it or anything in it (never a finger).

- `focusWithin?: BoxStyle;`

  Containers: focus on something in it.

- `enter?: BoxStyle;`

  What a widget appears from (since API\_MINOR 12, CSS `@starting-style`): built for the first time, or again after a frame without it, it starts with this on top and transitions to its look. Needs a `transition`. Skipped under reduced motion.

- `exit?: BoxStyle;`

  What a widget leaves toward (since API\_MINOR 12): one with this block that stops being built keeps drawing its last frame's drawing (its children included) while it transitions toward its look with this on top, then goes. Only `opacity`, `translate`, `scale` and `rotate` move in an exit (it replays drawing); it takes no input, focus or accessibility node and draws above the rest of its layer. Needs a `transition` (this block may give its own). Skipped under reduced motion. A dialog and its `backdrop` part take both: build the dialog only while it is open.

## Motion (since API\_MINOR 12)

Transitions, keyframe animations and enter and exit looks, as CSS's `transition`, `animation`, `@keyframes` and `@starting-style`, on the UI's clock (the frame times the game's UI sees; the same natively and in browsers). When a widget's resolved look changes (a state, a class, a token), each property group whose value changed moves from what shows toward the new value over the transition naming it; a group no transition names changes at once, and so does anything that is not a group (padding, sizes, fonts). A transition interrupted on its way back reverses from where it is, as long as it took to get there (as CSS's). Colors mix premultiplied; a color blends with a gradient, gradients of one type with as many stops blend, other fills switch; shadows and decorations pair by index, a missing one transparent. Motion follows widget ids (a label's, its text).

The player's reduced motion: transitions are instant, enter and exit skipped, and animations show their `rest`. `preferences().reducedMotion` and `engine.preferences().reducedMotion` agree in every frame.

Cost: widgets without motion in their styles keep no state; at most 512 widgets move at once (later ones jump to their target, their animations rest). While a shadow's blur or spread moves it takes steps of 2 logical pixels (each baked once into the skin cache), its exact value when the motion ends.

### TransitionProperty

*type*

```ts
export type TransitionProperty =
  | "all" | "background" | "border" | "radius" | "shadow" | "opacity"
  | "translate" | "scale" | "rotate" | "transform" | "text" | "focusRing"
  | "decorations" | "decorations.fill" | "decorations.position"
  | "decorations.opacity" | "decorations.rotate";
```

What a transition names (`properties`): `"all"`, a style key whose values move, `"transform"` (translate, scale and rotate), or a part of the decorations.

### Easing

*type*

```ts
export type Easing =
  | "linear" | "ease" | "ease-in" | "ease-out" | "ease-in-out" | "step-start" | "step-end"
  | { cubicBezier: readonly [number, number, number, number] }
  | { steps: number; position?: "start" | "end" };
```

A timing function, as CSS's: x1 and x2 of a cubic Bézier within 0–1 (RangeError), y free (overshoot); `steps` jumps at each step's end (`position: "start"`: at its start).

### Transition

*interface*

A transition: seconds (at most an hour; a negative duration is a RangeError). A negative delay starts it partway. Without `properties` it is every group's; in a list, a later one wins for a group both name (at most 16): `[{ properties: "decorations.opacity", duration: 0.16 }, { properties: "decorations.position", duration: 0.2, easing: { cubicBezier: [0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1] } }]`. A number is `{ duration }`.

```ts
export interface Transition { … }
```

- `duration: number;`

- `easing?: Easing;`

  Default `"ease"`.

- `delay?: number;`
- `properties?: TransitionProperty | readonly TransitionProperty[];`

### Animation

*interface*

A keyframe animation by its keyframes' name (`setAnimations`). It starts when a widget first shows it (or the name changes) and plays over its transitions. Keyframes without a `0%` (`from`) or `100%` (`to`) take the widget's current look at those ends, as CSS's implicit keyframes do: its state included (selected, hovered…), not only its classes. A pulse of `{ "50%": { shadow: glow } }` on a selected card therefore runs between the card's selected look and the glow; name the ends (`"0%, 100%": { shadow: rest }`) to fix them whatever the state.

```ts
export interface Animation { … }
```

- `name: string;`

- `duration: number;`

  Seconds an iteration (default 0).

- `iterations?: number | "infinite";`

  A count (fractions allowed, default 1) or `"infinite"`.

- `direction?: "normal" | "reverse" | "alternate" | "alternate-reverse";`

- `easing?: Easing;`

  Between each two keyframes, as CSS's animation-timing-function (default `"ease"`; a keyframe's own `easing` wins).

- `delay?: number;`

- `fill?: "none" | "forwards" | "backwards" | "both";`

  What shows before it starts and after it ends (default `"none"`: the widget's own look).

- `stagger?: number;`

  Seconds more delay for each child before the widget in its container: a menu's buttons cascading in (`stagger: 0.07`).

- `playState?: "running" | "paused";`

  `"paused"` freezes it where it is (as CSS; since API\_MINOR 12 not back at its delay's point), and `"running"` again carries on from there; one that starts paused holds where its delay puts it (a negative delay: that far in).

- `rest?: number;`

  The keyframe offset (0–1) shown under reduced motion; by default where it ends (an infinite one, where one iteration ends).

### Keyframe

*type*

```ts
export type Keyframe = Pick<
    BoxStyle,
    "background" | "border" | "radius" | "shadow" | "opacity" | "translate" | "scale" | "rotate" | "text" | "focusRing" | "decorations"
  > & { easing?: Easing };
```

A keyframe: the groups that move (anything else is a TypeError) and the easing to the next.

### setAnimations

*function*

```ts
export function setAnimations(animations: { readonly [name: string]: { readonly [offset: string]: Keyframe } }): void;
```

Registers keyframe animations by name (since API\_MINOR 12, CSS `@keyframes`): offsets `"from"`, `"to"` and percentages (`"50%"`, several comma-separated). A group a keyframe at an end does not set takes the widget's own value there. A name registered again is replaced. At most 32 keyframes a name, 256 names (RangeError) and 256 KiB of JSON a call; a call that throws registers nothing. A style naming an animation not registered adds nothing (one warning).

### CustomProperties

*type*

```ts
export type CustomProperties = { readonly [name: `--${string}`]: unknown };
```

Custom properties (since API\_MINOR 26; CSS's `--name: value`): any style or state block may declare `"--name": value`, and any value in a style may be `"var(--name)"` or `"var(--name, fallback)"` (the fallback a number or text: a color, a percentage, a token, another `var()`). A widget's `var()` resolves to its own rules' declarations (later rules and active state blocks winning), else its containers' (a container's base declarations are inherited by everything built inside it, the innermost winning), else the token of that name (`setTokens`, CSS's `:root`), else the fallback; with none, the property is ignored with one warning. A `var()` replaces a whole value (`"var(--gap)"`, not `"calc(…)"` or `"1px var(--c)"`). Older minors warn and ignore declarations and properties using `var()`.

### Style

*interface*

```ts
export interface Style extends BoxStyle, StateStyles { … }
```

- `extends?: string | readonly string[];`

  Keys this one builds on, flattened when registered (they must be registered before, or in the same call).

- `inside?: { readonly [key: string]: Style };`

  Rules for descendants, as CSS's `.speed button`: keys are kinds or classes; they nest up to 4 deep.

- `parts?: { readonly [part in PartName]?: BoxStyle & StateStyles };`

  The parts of a compound widget (since API\_MINOR 12; see `PartName`): each a box and text style with state blocks, in the widget's state (`option` and `tab` in their own). An unknown part throws a TypeError.

### setStyles

*function*

```ts
export function setStyles(styles: { readonly [key: string]: Style }): void;
```

Registers styles under their keys: a widget kind (`"button"`) sets its defaults, `".name"` a class. A key registered again is replaced. At most 512 keys (RangeError) and 256 KiB of JSON a call. Since API\_MINOR 37 a key may end in size conditions (`".panel@compact"`; see "Size classes"), each such key counting toward the 512.

### setTokens

*function*

```ts
export function setTokens(tokens: { readonly [name: string]: ColorLike | number | string | Fill | Shadow | readonly Shadow[] | Corners }): void;
```

The values `"$name"` stands for anywhere in a style: colors, numbers (corners, sizes), font names, fills and shadows. A changed token restyles every widget using it (a side's colors, a day/night palette) without registering styles again. At most 512 tokens.

### style

*function*

```ts
export function style(...styles: readonly (string | Style | false | null | undefined)[]): typeof import("starhermit:ui");
```

Classes (with or without the dot; several in one string separated by spaces) and inline style objects for the next widget or container, later ones winning; falsy entries are skipped: `ui.style("tool", active && "active").button(name)`. Chains with `id` either way round. The next widget or container takes what is chained (`style`, `id`, `tooltip`) whether or not it uses it (a spacer drops it), so it never reaches the one after. A class with no style registered is skipped (one warning). Prefer registered classes to inline objects, which are checked each call.

## From CSS (since API\_MINOR 12)

A port's style sheet as styles, ready to register:

```text
const css = ui.stylesFromCss(files.readText("theme/style.css"), { path: "theme/style.css" });
ui.setTokens(css.tokens); ui.setAnimations(css.animations); ui.setStyles(css.styles);
```

and `ui.row(label, build, css.layouts[".speed"])` where a container was `display: flex` or `grid`. The engine reads the CSS itself and never throws on it: what has no style is left out and listed in `dropped` with the reason. `starhermit css FILE` writes the same result as JSON, for a port to convert once and commit (read it back with `files.readJson`). What maps and what is dropped: the spec's "From CSS" section.

Selectors: the types the UI has kinds for (`button`; `label` and `span` as `label`; `p` as `paragraph`; `input` as `textField`, `slider` (`[type=range]`) or `checkbox`; `textarea`, `select`, `dialog`, `img`, `progress`, `meter`; `table` as `grid`; `tr`, `td`, `th` as the classes `tr`, `td`, `th` for a grid's `rowStyle` and `cellStyle`), `h1`–`h6` as the classes `h1`–`h6` since API\_MINOR 16 (one heading kind: `ui.style("h2").heading(text)`; games declaring an older `engine.minor` get every level as the `heading` kind), classes, a compound of classes (`.a.b`) as the class `"a.b"` (name it last: `ui.style("a", "b", "a.b")`), a type with a class as the class, since API\_MINOR 16 an id with no class (`#menu`, `button#go`) as the class of its name (`ui.style("menu")`, each listed in `dropped`; dropped for an older `engine.minor`), and descendants (`.speed button`, also `>`) as `inside` rules up to 3 deep. `:hover` (on a container kind, `hoverWithin`), `:active`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, `:focus-within`, `:disabled`, `:checked`, `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:nth-child(odd)` and `(even)` are state blocks, as are `.active`, `[aria-selected=true]` and `[aria-pressed=true]` (`selected`), `[aria-checked=true]` (`checked`) and `[aria-disabled=true]`; a scope's state moves to the styled key's block (`.tool.active .icon` is `".tool": { inside: { ".icon": { selected } } }`). `::before` and `::after` with `content: ""` and `position: absolute` are decorations; `::backdrop` and the range and progress pseudo-elements are parts. `:root` custom properties are tokens, and `var(--name)` stands as `"$name"` where its value fits.

The cascade: declarations for one key and state cascade as CSS's (specificity, then order; `!important` is ignored and listed); across keys the style cascade's order holds (kind, then `inside` rules, then classes in the order named), CSS's for type &lt; descendant &lt; class. A descendant rule for a class that the class's own rule also sets loses in the style cascade though CSS's is more specific: it is listed in `dropped` as shadowed.

Sizes: styles are border-box, so a rule's content-box `width`, `height`, `min-width` and `min-height` grow by its padding and border. Content-box is CSS's default; a rule's own `box-sizing`, else `*`'s, says otherwise. Since API\_MINOR 16 `*`'s is that of `*` itself (with `*::before, *::after`, which alone size no element) or, with `inherit`, of `html` or `:root`; with no `*` rule `button`, `select` and checkboxes are border-box as in browsers; and what it cannot decide (a `box-sizing: inherit` on a rule, a value it cannot read) is listed in `dropped`. Games declaring an older `engine.minor` read any `*` rule's (pseudo-elements' too) as border-box or not, and nothing else. `starhermit css` converts as the newest minor unless given `--minor N`.

### CssOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface CssOptions { … }
```

- `fontSize?: number;`

  Logical pixels of `rem` (and of `em` where a rule gives no font size): by default the sheet's own `:root` or `html` font size, else the theme's default.

- `fonts?: readonly string[];`

  The families the game adds with `canvas.fonts`: a `font-family` list takes the first of these, else its first generic family.

- `path?: string;`

  The sheet's path in the package, which its `url()`s are relative to (default the root).

### CssDropped

*interface*

What has no style, or is styled other than as written (an id as a class, since API\_MINOR 16), and why.

```ts
export interface CssDropped { … }
```

- `readonly selector: string;`

- `readonly property: string;`

  The declaration's property (empty for a whole rule).

- `readonly value: string;`
- `readonly reason: string;`

- `readonly line: number;`

  From 1; 0 for what was found once converted.

### CssLayout

*type*

```ts
export type CssLayout = Layout &
  Partial<Pick<GridLayout, "columns" | "rows" | "gap">> & { container?: "row" | "column" | "grid" };
```

A container's layout from `display: flex` or `grid` (with `flex-direction`, `justify-content`, `align-items`, `gap`, `flex-grow`, `grid-template-columns` and `-rows`): `container` names the call that takes it, which ignores the field.

### CssStyles

*interface*

```ts
export interface CssStyles { … }
```

- `readonly styles: { readonly [key: string]: Style };`
- `readonly animations: { readonly [name: string]: { readonly [offset: string]: Keyframe } };`
- `readonly tokens: { readonly [name: string]: ColorLike | number | string | Fill | Shadow | readonly Shadow[] };`
- `readonly layouts: { readonly [key: string]: CssLayout };`
- `readonly dropped: readonly CssDropped[];`

### stylesFromCss

*function*

```ts
export function stylesFromCss(css: string, options?: CssOptions): CssStyles;
```

Converts a style sheet (at most 1 MiB, RangeError): plain objects for `setStyles`, `setAnimations` and `setTokens`, which take them as they are. Not a TypeError for any CSS. Needs no frame: convert once, at the start. Since API\_MINOR 28 it converts what API\_MINOR 26 added to styles (`starhermit css --minor 26` does so ahead of time): custom properties on any selector as `"--name"` declarations, `var()`s of them as `"var(--name)"`, percentage sizes, `max-width` and `max-height`, `font-variant: small-caps` as `text.variant`, and `flex-wrap` as a row's `wrap` with its `gap`.

### UiPreferences

*interface*

What the player's settings make of the UI this frame (since API\_MINOR 11): `scale` is window pixels per logical pixel (the window's scale factor times the player's interface size), `textScale` the player's text size on top of it for text, and whether colors are high-contrast and motion reduced. Read it each frame: it changes when the window moves to another display or the player changes a setting (`engine.onPreferencesChange` tells of the latter). A new frozen object each call.

```ts
export interface UiPreferences { … }
```

- `readonly scale: number;`
- `readonly textScale: number;`
- `readonly highContrast: boolean;`
- `readonly reducedMotion: boolean;`

### preferences

*function*

```ts
export function preferences(): UiPreferences;
```

## Size classes (since API\_MINOR 37)

What kind of screen to lay out for, at breakpoints every game shares (Material 3's window classes), from the logical viewport: the window inside its safe area (`frame().safeArea`), divided by `preferences().scale`, so a larger interface size moves a game to a smaller class as a browser's zoom does. Width: `"compact"` below 600 logical pixels (a phone upright), `"medium"` from 600 (a phone on its side, a small tablet, a narrow window), `"expanded"` from 840 (a tablet on its side, a laptop's window), `"large"` from 1200 (a desktop). Height: `"compact"` below 480 (a phone on its side), `"medium"` from 480, `"expanded"` from 900. `"landscape"` when wider than tall (a square is portrait).

Styles follow them: a key may name conditions after `@`, and its rule applies right after the key's own (before the next class) while every condition holds, as CSS's `@media` rules: `".panel@compact"`, `"button@landscape@short"`. Conditions: a width class (`compact`, `medium`, `expanded`, `large`), a width class or wider (`medium+`, `expanded+`, `large+`: CSS's `min-width`), `portrait`, `landscape`, `short` (the compact height class) and `tall` (the expanded one). An unknown condition is a TypeError; a class with only conditioned rules is styled where they hold and warns nowhere.
