They follow the frame's classes, so a resize or a new interface size restyles from the next frame. Games declaring an older `engine.minor` have neither `viewport` nor `breakpoints`, and `@` stays part of a class's name.

### WidthClass

*type*

```ts
export type WidthClass = "compact" | "medium" | "expanded" | "large";
```

### HeightClass

*type*

```ts
export type HeightClass = "compact" | "medium" | "expanded";
```

### Viewport

*interface*

```ts
export interface Viewport { … }
```

- `readonly x: number;`

  The safe area's inner box in logical pixels, from the window's top-left (`x`, `y` are the safe area's left and top insets).

- `readonly y: number;`
- `readonly width: number;`
- `readonly height: number;`

- `readonly scale: number;`

  Window pixels per logical pixel, as `preferences().scale`.

- `readonly widthClass: WidthClass;`
- `readonly heightClass: HeightClass;`
- `readonly orientation: "portrait" | "landscape";`

### viewport

*const*

```ts
export const viewport: (() => Viewport) | undefined;
```

The frame's logical viewport and its size classes (a new frozen object each call): what games worked out themselves as `(frame().width - safeArea.left - safeArea.right) / ui.preferences().scale`. Since API\_MINOR 37; undefined before.

### breakpoints

*const*

```ts
export const breakpoints:
  | {
      readonly width: { readonly medium: 600; readonly expanded: 840; readonly large: 1200 };
      readonly height: { readonly medium: 480; readonly expanded: 900 };
    }
  | undefined;
```

The breakpoints in logical pixels: where `medium`, `expanded` and `large` widths and `medium` and `expanded` heights begin (`{ width: { medium: 600, expanded: 840, large: 1200 }, height: { medium: 480, expanded: 900 } }`, frozen). Since API\_MINOR 37; undefined before.

## Toasts (since API\_MINOR 37)

Short notifications the engine queues, times, stacks and draws over the game's UI (and its dialogs), whether or not the frame builds any widgets: "Saved", "Invite link copied", "Connection lost". At most 3 show at once in each stack, the bottom one (the default, the newest nearest the bottom edge) and the top one (the newest nearest the top); more wait in order, each one's time starting as it shows, and past 32 waiting the oldest waiting is dropped. Each shows for `duration` seconds; by default 3 (info, success) or 5 (warning, error), or as long as its text takes to read (15 characters a second) up to 10, whichever is longer; 0 (or Infinity) keeps it until dismissed. The pointer resting on one keeps it up. A press and release on a dismissible one (the default) dismisses it; the UI takes that press (`ui.pointerOver()` and `ui.pointerCaptured()` are true over it, and `input.onGesture` makes no gesture of it), while one with `dismissible: false` lets the pointer through.

They follow the player's settings: the UI's scale and text size, high contrast (the forced look of every box), reduced motion (no fade or slide: they appear and go at once), and they stay inside the window's safe area. The engine's look is a dark rounded box with the kind's accent as its border (blue, green, amber, red) and light text; `style` gives the toast the game's own instead, as `ui.style(…)` takes it (class names, style objects, or a list of them): its box, padding and text color. Each toast is a label in the accessibility tree and, unless `announce: false`, a screen reader announces it as it shows (politely; warnings and errors assertively), as `ui.announce` would: a game that announced its own toasts drops that call. Times run on the game's clock (`frame().time`), so a play script and a replay see the same toasts in the same frames. Games declaring an older `engine.minor` have neither `toast` nor `clearToasts`.

### ToastKind

*type*

```ts
export type ToastKind = "info" | "success" | "warning" | "error";
```

### ToastOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface ToastOptions { … }
```

- `kind?: ToastKind;`

  Default `"info"`; another value is a TypeError.

- `duration?: number;`

  Seconds it shows once it shows (0 or Infinity: until dismissed; at most 3600, RangeError; a negative or non-number is a TypeError). Default: the kind's time or the reading time.

- `dismissible?: boolean;`

  A press on it dismisses it (default true).

- `position?: "top" | "bottom";`

  The stack it shows in (default `"bottom"`).

- `anchor?: "left" | "center" | "right";`

  Since API\_MINOR 38 (`TOAST_PLACEMENT_MINOR`; not read before): where across the safe area its stack stands (default `"center"`; the margin in from that side for left and right). Another value is a TypeError.

- `offset?: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 38 (not read before): logical pixels its stack starts in from its edge past the margin, to clear a HUD or a tray (0 to 4096, RangeError; a non-number is a TypeError; default 0). Toasts with the same position, anchor and offset share a stack of 3; at most 8 stacks show at once, and a toast of another stack waits (as a full stack's do) until one empties.

- `announce?: boolean;`

  Screen readers announce it as it shows (default true).

- `style?: string | Style | readonly (string | Style)[];`

  The game's look for its box and text instead of the engine's, as `ui.style(…)` takes it. Since API\_MINOR 41 (`TOAST_STYLE_MINOR`) its text sets as a label's (`font`, `weight`, `align` for each wrapped line, spacing, transform, shadows), `maxWidth` replaces the 28-em cap (a percentage is of the safe area's width) and `minWidth`/`minHeight` widen the box; before, the text drew in the UI's first font, regular, from the box's start, at most 28 ems wide. Since API\_MINOR 41 toasts also stack in the window less its safe area whatever `setViewport` moved the UI to that frame (before, in the last viewport set, so opening a screen in a panel's rectangle moved them).

### Toast

*interface*

```ts
export interface Toast { … }
```

- `readonly id: number;`

- `dismiss(): boolean;`

  Fades it out (a waiting one goes at once); false when it is no longer queued.

- `readonly queued: boolean;`

  Showing or waiting: not dismissed, timed out or cleared.

### toast

*const*

```ts
export const toast: ((text: string, options?: ToastOptions) => Toast | null) | undefined;
```

Queues a toast (since API\_MINOR 37): its handle, or null for blank text. At most 500 characters (RangeError). Undefined before.

### clearToasts

*const*

```ts
export const clearToasts: (() => void) | undefined;
```

Removes every toast at once, showing and waiting (since API\_MINOR 37; undefined before).

### measureText

*function*

```ts
export function measureText(
    text: string,
    options?: TextOptions & {
      width?: number;
      kind?: "label" | "heading" | "button";
      /** A widget in these classes and inline styles (since API_MINOR 12),
       * as `ui.style(…).button(text)` (or `label`, `heading`) lays it
       * out. */
      style?: string | Style | readonly (string | Style)[];
    },
  ): { width: number; height: number };
```

The size, in window pixels, that a widget with this text takes this frame (since API\_MINOR 11), within rounding of the rectangle it returns: a `label` (the default `kind`), a `heading`, or a `button` (its padding included); with `width` (logical pixels, a label's text only) a `paragraph` that wide: its height and its widest line (the paragraph's rectangle spans all of `width`). It measures with the current scale and text size, the options' size, font and weight, and the font (`setFont`) and text of the container it is called in. Counts as a UI call. A `width` with `kind: "button"` throws a TypeError, a non-finite one a RangeError. Since API\_MINOR 12 it measures as the widget draws: the kind's style (a `button` style's padding) and the container's `inside` rules count, with or without `style`.

## Richer widgets (since API\_MINOR 12)

### WidgetState

*interface*

What a `widget`'s `draw` gets after its rectangle.

```ts
export interface WidgetState { … }
```

- `readonly hovered: boolean;`
- `readonly pressed: boolean;`

- `readonly focused: boolean;`

  Any focus (the engine draws the ring for focus the player sees).

- `readonly disabled: boolean;`

- `readonly selected: boolean;`

  A checked checkbox or toggle, a chosen radio.

- `readonly value: number | null;`

  A slider's or meter's value after this frame's input; else null.

- `readonly scale: number;`

  Window pixels per logical pixel (`preferences().scale`).

- `readonly highContrast: boolean;`

  Draw with `colors`, which are the forced ones under high contrast.

- `readonly reducedMotion: boolean;`

- `readonly colors: { readonly text: string; readonly background: string; readonly accent: string; readonly border: string };`

  The `widget` style's colors (CSS `rgba()` strings), else the theme's for the state; the forced colors under high contrast.

### RegionPointer

*interface*

A region's pointer this frame, window pixels from its top-left.

```ts
export interface RegionPointer { … }
```

- `readonly x: number;`
- `readonly y: number;`

- `readonly inside: boolean;`

  Over the region (a drag that began in it keeps reporting outside).

- `readonly buttons: number;`

  Held: 1 primary, 2 secondary, 4 middle.

- `readonly dragX: number;`

  A drag that began in it: how far the pointer moved since last frame.

- `readonly dragY: number;`

- `readonly wheelX: number;`

  Wheel notches over it (the region takes them: scroll areas around it do not scroll).

- `readonly wheelY: number;`

### WidgetResult

*interface*

What a `widget` did this frame (a new frozen object each call).

```ts
export interface WidgetResult extends Rect { … }
```

- `readonly activated: boolean;`

  Clicked, or Enter, Space or South while focused (never disabled).

- `readonly secondary: boolean;`

  The secondary button pressed on it, or the context-menu key while it has focus.

- `readonly hovered: boolean;`

- `readonly entered: boolean;`

  The pointer came onto it or left it this frame.

- `readonly left: boolean;`

- `readonly pressed: boolean;`

  Held down.

- `readonly focused: boolean;`

- `readonly checked?: boolean;`

  Toggles, checkboxes and radios: on after this frame's activation.

- `readonly value?: number;`

  Sliders and meters: the value after this frame's input.

- `readonly pointer?: RegionPointer;`

  Regions: the pointer, and while focused the keys (`KeyboardEvent.code`) and gamepad controls (`"DpadLeft"`, `"South"`) pressed this frame.

- `readonly keys?: readonly string[];`

### WidgetSpec

*interface*

```ts
export interface WidgetSpec extends WidgetOptions { … }
```

- `role: "button" | "toggle" | "checkbox" | "radio" | "slider" | "meter" | "image" | "none" | "region";`

  What it is to input and screen readers:

  ```text
  "button"   activates (`activated`);
  "toggle"   a button announced pressed or not (`checked`), flipped
             on activation;
  "checkbox" as a toggle, announced as a checkbox;
  "radio"    chosen on activation; in a `radiogroup` container one
             of the group (arrows choose);
  "slider"   Left/Right step `value` by `step`, a press or drag sets
             it (on `min + k × step`);
  "meter"    shows `value`; takes no focus;
  "image"    takes no focus; the label is its description (empty:
             decorative);
  "none"     presentation: no node, no focus (a color swatch);
  "region"   an area that takes the pointer (`pointer`), and keys
             while focused (`keys`): a radar, a campaign map. With
             `arrows` it keeps the arrows and the D-pad instead of
             moving focus with them (Tab still leaves it: give
             gamepad players another way out).
  ```

- `size: { width: number; height: number };`

  Logical pixels.

- `draw?: (rect: Rect, state: WidgetState) => void;`

  Draws it, after its style's box and before its focus ring, with `starhermit:draw` (or `draw.box`): its rectangle (window pixels, the style's `translate` applied) and state. Its drawing goes where the widget is among the UI's (over widgets built before it, under those after), clipped as the widget is, and counts toward the overlay's items and text as `starhermit:draw` does. It draws only: building a widget in it throws a TypeError. Honour `state.highContrast` and `state.reducedMotion`.

- `style?: string | readonly string[];`

  Classes (styled as the `widget` kind).

- `disabled?: boolean;`
- `checked?: boolean;`
- `value?: number;`
- `min?: number;`
- `max?: number;`
- `step?: number;`

- `description?: string;`

  Read after the name ("Unlocks at 3 stars", "Campaign map: use the arrows to pan").

- `arrows?: boolean;`

### widget

*function*

```ts
export function widget(label: string, spec: WidgetSpec): WidgetResult;
```

A widget the game draws, with the engine's identity (its label, or `id()`), focus order, keyboard, gamepad and touch navigation, focus ring and accessibility node for its `role`: a board square, a cameo, a dial, a swatch, a map. Counts toward the widgets a frame.

### MeterOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface MeterOptions extends WidgetOptions { … }
```

- `min?: number;`

  The range (default 0–1); `max` below `min` is a RangeError.

- `max?: number;`

- `markers?: readonly number[];`

  Values marked across the bar (a threshold, a target), at most 16.

- `segments?: number;`

  Lit cells instead of a continuous fill, 0–64 (0: continuous).

- `indeterminate?: boolean;`

  Busy without a known value: a block sweeps along (resting in the middle with reduced motion), announced busy.

- `width?: number;`

  Logical pixels (default 200).

### meter

*function*

```ts
export function meter(label: string, value: number, options?: MeterOptions): Rect;
```

A gauge (power, fuel, a health bar) announced as a meter named `label` with its value and range. Styled as `meter`, its parts `track` and `fill` (each lit segment).

### document

*function*

```ts
export function document(label: string, text: string, build: () => void, layout?: Layout): Rect;
```

A sheet the game paints (a letter, orders, a newspaper) that screen readers read as `text`, in reading order: one document node named `label`. `build` lays out as a column (`layout` as a container's) and may draw anything; the nodes of what it builds give way to `text`, except widgets that take focus (a Sign button stays). Styled as `document`.

### setFont

*function*

```ts
export function setFont(font: { family?: string; weight?: FontWeight } | null): void;
```

The font the UI lays out and draws its text with: a family added with `canvas.fonts` (any case) at the face nearest `weight` (synthesized bold at 600 and more for a family without a bold face), falling back to the system's faces, or since API\_MINOR 8 a generic family (`serif`, `cursive`…, see `TextOptions.font`); null returns to the default faces (`system-ui`, see `starhermit:draw`). A family never added throws a TypeError.

## Retained subtrees (since API\_MINOR 41, `RETAIN_MINOR`)

A part of the UI that changes only now and then (a HUD page, a selection card, a sidebar of `starhermit:draw` items) need not run its script every frame. `retain(key, version, build)` runs `build` and records every `starhermit:ui` and `starhermit:draw` call it makes (the arguments as read, what each returned, the calls inside each container); on later frames it makes the same calls again natively, without calling `build`, while:

- `version` (a number or a string the game changes whenever what `build` shows changes) is the same;
- the subtree is laid out where it was: the same container state (its cursor, sizes and children before it), clip, scroll offset, viewport, window size, UI scale and text size, theme, language, styles, tokens and animations (`setStyles`, `setTokens`, `setAnimations`, `setTheme` and `setFont` make it build again), fonts, contrast, and the `id`, `style` or text tooltip chained onto its first widget;
- the reads it made answer the same (`focused`, `capturingKeys`, `pointerOver`, `pointerCaptured`, `preferences`, `viewport`, `submitted`, and `back` with no Back waiting);
- and no input this frame could make one of its calls return otherwise (Input, below).

A record replays once two builds in a row recorded the same calls, so a subtree builds on its first two frames, twice after each change, and every frame while it changes by itself (a scroll area gliding).

The UI gets the same calls in the same order either way, so widget ids, layout, hover and press looks, focus rings, transitions and animations, tooltips, scrolling, the accessibility tree, play scripts' targets and the frame's call and item budgets are what issuing them gives. Retained and issued calls interleave freely: siblings before and after it, containers around it, retains inside retains (an inner key replays inside its outer's build, so a page key holding panel keys builds only the panel that changed), a retain inside a scroll area and scroll areas inside a retain. `retain` adds no container and no id scope: its calls are placed and named as if issued where it is.

Input: `build` runs, and its widgets answer there as they always do (`if (ui.button("Buy")) buy()`), on every frame where an input could change what one of its calls returns: a press, release or secondary press on one of its rectangles (one between them, over none, replays), a drag that began on one, the wheel over one, keys, text or navigation while one of its widgets has focus or captures keys, an assistive technology's activation of one, NextTab or PreviousTab while it holds tabs, focus moving while it holds a scroll area, a scroll area of it still gliding, flung or dragged; any input at all while it holds a dialog, an open select or a custom `widget`, and for a custom widget also the pointer moving, a button or the focus changing. On the other frames nothing in it could return anything new, so it replays: no click, key or result is ever lost or delayed.

Rectangles: a replay hands nothing back to the game, but each replayed call returns what it returned when recorded (else the subtree builds): rectangles, scroll offsets and results the build kept (`const r = ui.label(…)`, kept for a tooltip or a minimap) stay right, and `lastRect()` after the retain is its last widget's, as issued.

The contract: what `build` shows follows from `version` and from what the UI returns it. Only `starhermit:ui` and `starhermit:draw` calls are recorded; anything else `build` does (changing game state, drawing into a canvas, playing a sound, reading input or the clock) happens only on the frames it runs. A tooltip builder (`tooltip: () => …`) and a custom widget's `draw` are the recorded build's functions, run live as the calls that took them run them. A replayed call that returns other than it did makes the next frame build.

Lifetime and limits: a key not issued in a frame is let go of, with its record and the functions it holds. At most 4,096 keys are kept at once, and all records together hold at most 32 MiB (their calls, arguments, results and nested keys' records, counted in every key holding them); past them a key builds every frame, unkept (the console says so once), and so does a key holding a nested key not kept. A call given a string longer than 1,048,576 UTF-16 units (more than any recordable native reads) is made unkept, and a key that built more than 4,096 widgets builds every frame. `retainStats()` tells how many keys are kept and how often they built and replayed. A key issued twice in a frame, a key that is not a string, a version neither a number nor a string, and a tooltip builder chained onto `retain` or left last in `build` for no widget are TypeErrors.

Fuel: a replay costs 4 instructions plus 1 for each call it makes again (nested ones included), the same every frame, where issuing spends 40 to 80 on each call's options in script besides `build`'s own work; natives that charge for their work (an uncached text layout, a path not kept) charge as when issued. A frame that builds costs what issuing does, and recording it a little native time (a key whose version changes every frame records only every fourth build past its second, and replays from the third frame after it settles). The browser's engine records and replays the same way, with the same frames.

### retain

*const*

```ts
export const retain: ((key: string, version: number | string, build: () => void) => boolean) | undefined;
```

Records `build`'s calls and makes them again natively, without calling `build`, while `version`, the place it is laid out in and the input reaching it stay the same (see above). True on a frame `build` ran. Undefined for games declaring an older `engine.minor`.

### retainStats

*const*

```ts
export const retainStats:
  | (() => {
      keys: number;
      confirmed: number;
      calls: number;
      bytes: number;
      builds: number;
      replays: number;
      mismatches: number;
    })
  | undefined;
```

What `retain` keeps (both modules' keys, `ui.retain`'s and `draw.retain`'s): `keys` kept and of them `confirmed` (replaying when nothing reaches them), the `calls` and `bytes` their records hold (at most 32 MiB), and the `builds`, `replays` and `mismatches` (replays where a call returned other than recorded, so the next frame built) since the game started. Undefined for games declaring an older `engine.minor`.
